One answer. That's all SCOPEY needed. Now it writes — and it doesn't stop at a title and a sentence. Every scope has four parts: Why it's needed, What it does exactly, What could go wrong, and What it must not break. The person who builds it has no excuses. Neither does the person who reviews it.

📄 SCOPEY — REQ-0047 · Preferred Contact Method Field

Why

PMs need to know how clients want to be reached. Right now it lives in someone's head — or worse, an email no one can find.

What

Optional picklist "Preferred Contact Method" — Email / Phone / Slack / Teams — on both the New Project and Edit Project pages.

What could go wrong

· Field left blank → project saves, no error

· Existing records → field shows empty, not broken

What it must not break [...] What it must not break

· Existing project layout and page rules stay intact

· No validation rule — this field is never required

### 📋 Your Requirement Style — your structure, your rules, every time

No two businesses scope work the same way. A software consultancy doesn't write requirements like a product team. A fixed-fee project doesn't need the same sections as a T&M retainer. SCOPEY reads its instructions from the Agentforce Agent Resource — plus specific instructions you write in plain language, directly on the project record. No code. No configuration files. Just tell SCOPEY how you want it to write. That means every project type gets its own output structure. Your sections. Your labels. Your level of detail. # SCOPEY 1AI Business Analysis Agent for Salesforce

Bad requirements cost weeks. They cause rework, missed deadlines, and deliverables that don't match what the business needed. SCOPEY stops that at the source.

Stop building the wrong thing.
